author: Nick Robins-Early
description:
Justice department had ordered state to segregate and not count 20,000 ballots from people it claims are non-citizens

  • US midterms – live updates

The supreme court on Monday ruled against the Trump administration and its attempts to force California election officials to segregate and not count ballots from people that the justice department claims are non-citizens. The ruling follows several lower courts siding with California officials, who argued the federal government was seeking to interfere in state elections.

California and the Trump administration have been in a legal standoff over the past few weeks following the justice department’s claim that 20,000 non-citizens were on the state’s voter rolls. The DoJ delivered a USB drive to Los Angeles and Sacramento election officia
title: Supreme court rules against Trump over bid to force California to set aside ballots

author: Anna Betts
description:
Individual, who also had underlying conditions, was hospitalized after being exposed to avian influenza

A Washington state resident has died after being hospitalized with “severe illness” after contracting bird flu, local health officials said on Sunday.

The individual was exposed to avian influenza, also known as bird flu, at a dairy with infected cattle in Yakima county, according to a news release. The person was subsequently hospitalized with severe illness and died on Sunday. Health officials said that the individual, whose identity had not been released, had underlying health conditions.

Continue reading...
title: Washington state resident dies from ‘severe illness’ after contracting bird flu

author: Ariana Baio
description:
US president shares delayed results of chaotic renovation on DC site as Americans prepare to head to the polls

Donald Trump unveiled the delayed results of his $14m renovation of Washington DC’s Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool in what is expected to be his final press conference before voters head to the polls for the midterm elections.

On the eve of a consequential election day, with polls indicating that most voters feel the US president has grown too focused on building projects in the nation’s capital, he stood in front of the newly opened reflecting pool to discuss – in detail – changes to the pool’s pipe, the grass surrounding the area and granite.

Continue reading...
title: Trump unveils results of $14m reflecting pool makeover in final appeal before midterms

author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
description:
While PM is keen to support those making a contribution his backing of Shabana Mahmood’s hard line is no surprise

While out on the campaign trail in Makerfield, Andy Burnham gave a glimpse into where he might land on Labour’s plans for immigration reform, which had already been decried by the left of the party as unfair and the right as electorally necessary.

Asked by the Guardian what he thought of Reform’s attack on “open borders Andy” – Nigel Farage’s early attempt to define him as soft on migration – the then Manchester mayor dismissed the charge as “ridiculous” and went on the defensive.

Continue reading...
title: Migration is a moral issue for Burnham – but he also wants to tell a positive story

author: Maya Yang
description:
Her latest plea comes three months after urging ‘someone to come forward’ with details about Nancy Guthrie

Savannah Guthrie has issued a new plea for help on the whereabouts of her 84-year-old mother, who authorities believe was abducted in February.

On Sunday, the Today show co-host shared a photo of an old drawing made by her daughter featuring an umbrella and the words: “I know it might not seem like it but I really need my mommy.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘We cannot move forward’: Savannah Guthrie shares new post seeking information in mother’s disappearance

author: Joseph Gedeon in Detroit, Michigan
description:
The issue runs through almost every twist and turn and has come to define the congresswoman’s political persona

For Haley Stevens, the road from Democratic Senate candidate to campaigning alongside a Republican she once called a rubber stamp for Donald Trump has been remarkably short – and the issue running through almost every twist and turn has been Israel.

Having failed to stop Abdul El-Sayed in the primary, Stevens chose to back Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday, a candidate who she previously warned would enable Trump’s agenda – apparently because the Democrat who won refuses to share her position on Israel.

Continue reading...
title: How Israel is at the heart of Haley Stevens’s extraordinary reversal

author: Robert Booth and Miatta Mbriwa
description:
After a second apparent cyber-attack in as many weeks, we examine possible culprits and their motives

  • Shop fridges and freezers across Europe hit by fresh suspected cyber-attack

Supermarket fridges and freezers in seven European countries have malfunctioned, their thermostats remotely cranked up in some cases to 50C (122F).

The EU has condemned what it said was “a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine consumers’ confidence in it”.

Continue reading...
title: Who is hacking Europe’s supermarket fridges and freezers, and why?

author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
description:
The husband, who cannot be named to protect his victim, has already pleaded guilty to a number of offences carried out at the couple’s Stockport home

Nine men have gone on trial accused of being involved in the abuse of a woman who was drugged, raped and sexually assaulted by her husband while he “lived a double life masked in respectability”.

The husband, who cannot be named in order to protect the anonymity of his victim, has already pleaded guilty to a number of offences against his wife spanning more than two decades.

Continue reading...
title: Trial of nine men accused of abusing woman drugged and raped by husband begins

author: Ariana Baio
description:
The two FBI agents were charged with making false statements to Congress while testifying about the bureau’s role in investigating Biden’s laptop

A federal judge dismissed criminal charges against two former FBI officials who were accused of lying about their involvement in the investigation into Hunter Biden, the son of former president Joe Biden, on Monday.

Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said prosecutors failed to show probable cause that the two former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, had knowingly made false statements.

Continue reading...
title: Judge tosses case against two officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden

author: Chris Stein in Wever, Iowa
description:
Residents would welcome the development, but the president’s past false promises cast doubt on the proposal

On a Monday afternoon in late September, Donald Trump gathered Iowa Republicans in the Oval Office to make a big announcement: the firm Mesabi Metallics would invest $15bn to make the midwestern state the site of the largest steel mill in the country.

One month later, and just days before the midterm election, word has spread in the small town of Wever, population 142, that the mill will be built somewhere nearby. And that’s been about it – no shovels in the dirt, workers on a job site or machinery on the dirt roads leading down towards the Mississippi River.

Continue reading...
title: Trump promised a steel mill in this rural Iowa region. But is it all a midterm election ploy?

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Connor Sanderson-Doyle is one of four men accused of sexually abusing Joanne Young, who was repeatedly assaulted by her husband, Philip Young

A man has told a court he believed a woman who was repeatedly raped and drugged by her husband had consented when he answered an advert to have sex with her.

Former Tory councillor Philip Young has pleaded guilty to multiple charges of drugging and sexually abusing his wife, Joanne Young, during a 13-year period at their home in Swindon, Wiltshire.

Continue reading...
title: Defendant tells court he believed he had consent of woman drugged by her husband

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
Trust admits Danielle Brown’s baby would have survived had she not been sent home from RVI days earlier

A woman whose unborn baby had died was sent home from hospital with a booklet for bereaved parents and told to book a slot to give birth.

Danielle Brown, 31, was seven months pregnant when she was first discharged from hospital with pre-eclampsia, a potentially life-threatening pregnancy complication. She returned to hospital days later, when scans revealed that her daughter, Maisie, had died.

Continue reading...
title: Newcastle hospital told woman whose unborn baby had died to go home and ‘book a slot to give birth’

author: Joe Pinner
description:
Devon nature reserve says ‘reckless’ theft of narrow-headed ant colony sets back years of conservation work

A nest containing up to 5,000 of England’s rarest ant species has been stolen from a nature reserve, a conservation charity has said.

Devon Wildlife Trust (DWT) said a nest of narrow-headed ants had been dug up and taken from Chudleigh Knighton Heath nature reserve in south Devon, which is the last place in England where the species still exists.

Continue reading...
title: Rare ant nest stolen from last place in England where species survives

author: Josh Butler
description:
Growing disdain for gambling and animal cruelty concerns drive sliding interest in race that once ‘stopped the nation’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne Cup, with more than two-thirds surveyed saying they have low or zero interest in the annual horse race.

Support for the Melbourne Cup has been sliding consistently for a number of years, but the Guardian Essential poll found just 9% of Australians said they had high interest in the race now – nearly half the proportion in 2025.
title: Guardian Essential poll: record number of Australians are turning their backs on the Melbourne Cup

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Exclusive: Shoalhaven council says Wall of Tears installation by Phil Buehler posed risk to staff, visitors and tenants

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A New South Wales local council has refused to show a world-renowned artwork about children killed in Gaza after asking organisers to investigate hiring “armed guards” to counter the risk of “community conflict” over the mural.

The group, Shoalhaven Friends of Palestine, was aiming to show the Wall of Tears installation by American artist Phil Buehler at the Shoalhaven Regional Gallery in No
title: NSW council refuses to show world-renowned Gaza artwork over ‘unacceptable’ safety risk

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Social network and Digital Freedom Project, led by NSW state MP John Ruddick, seek to overturn ban on grounds of implied freedom of political communication

Australia’s world-leading under-16s social media ban will face its first major legal challenge on Tuesday, as Reddit and an advocacy group headed by a libertarian politician seek to overturn the law in the high court.

Nearly 11 months ago, 10 platforms – Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Kick, X, Twitch and Threads – were required to deactivate or suspend the accounts of users they determined to be aged under 16 years.

Continue reading...
title: Reddit and libertarian group challenge Australia’s under-16s social media ban in high court

author: Guardian staff
description:
Patient with chest pains rescued by Cleveland EMS after driver of private ambulance gets lost and leaves

An ambulance driver in Ohio abandoned a patient they were taking to hospital after getting lost and decided to call an Uber and go home.

The bizarre incident played out in Cleveland last week when the patient was being transported to the Cleveland Clinic with chest pain. According to the local broadcaster KWTX: “The ambulance driver got lost, told her he was done driving for the day, and called an Uber.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘Done for the day’: US ambulance driver abandons patient and takes Uber home

author: Hilary Beaumont
description:
Concerns about datacenters and high energy bills could help Democrats clinch races in Ohio, Arizona and Michigan

In Arizona, where summer temperatures regularly hit triple digits, air conditioning can be a matter of life and death. This year, as the state recorded its hottest summer on record, Diali Avila’s monthly power bill went up to $400, the highest it has ever been.

Avila, the state director for Climate Power, an advocacy group, said the upcoming elections offered voters an opportunity to elect candidates who can ease their utility bills. “People are making the connection: they’re looking at their electricity bills that they get at the end of the month, and then they’re looking at their ballot, and the
title: ‘Politics of electricity’ over rising bills could power Democratic win, say clean energy advocates

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Prospect to hold workplace sessions and recruit members under agreement with tech company

Trade unions are expected to make further inroads into big tech companies in the UK after new rights for unions to access workplaces came into force, with Google UK signing an agreement on Monday.

Prospect union has reached an agreement with Google to begin organising among about 7,000 workers across its UK operations, including YouTube but excluding DeepMind.

Continue reading...
title: Unions gain access to thousands of Google workers after UK employment rights overhaul

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Letter from mayor tells federal agents to stay out of city-owned facilities for immigration operations

Mayor Zohran Mamdani has threatened to take legal action against Immigration and Customs Enforcement over allegations the agency’s officers at the agency are using parking lots owned by New York City for operations in the area.

In a letter to the Trump administration, Mamdani noted the agency’s use of property owned by the city was “unauthorized and is therefore illegal, endangers City residents, and sows fear among those who seek to access City property”.

Continue reading...
title: Mamdani threatens ICE with legal action over use of New York parking lots

author: Associated Press
description:
Mandatory evacuations in Arizona and New Mexico with Pagosa Springs warned of potentially ‘catastrophic’ deluge

Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding and mandatory evacuations in a swath of the south-west on Sunday, including in a Colorado tourist town bracing for its main river to rise to historic levels, as weary residents in the normally arid region deal with another drenching.

Officials in Pagosa Springs, a town of more than 2,000 in the Rockies located near ski resorts and known for its hot springs, warned of potentially “catastrophic flooding” as the San Juan River was forecast to crest at more than 20ft (6.1 meters) late on Sunday night.

Continue reading...
title: Colorado town braces for historic flood as heavy rains batter south-west

author: Martin Belam
description:
Trump called Democratic candidate a ‘jihadist’ as El-Sayed’s defeated primary opponent backs Republican Mike Rogers. Plus an Australian fish worth its weight in gold

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, has endorsed his Republican rival in an extraordinary rebuke of her party’s nominee on the eve of the midterm elections. Tensions between El-Sayed and Stevens had already led to him asking her to stay away from his campaign events, and her endorsement of Mike Rogers comes as the U
title: Stevens defects to back El-Sayed’s Michigan opponent as Trump delivers anti-Muslim tirade | First Thing

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
The latest move has roiled one of the most fiercely contested Senate contests

In his first public comments since Stevens’s endorsement of Rogers, El-Sayed told reporters at a press conference outside of a rally he held on Sunday, the very same rally that Stevens had earlier been disinvited from attending, “At the end of the day, I actually don’t think about Haley Stevens.” He added, “I’m just less interested in the politics of it all than I am in the policy of it all.

“If you are somebody who believes that we should stand up to hate, and you have watched this last campaign, I think we probably would not want to support Mike Rogers and Donald Trump and JD Vance,” he said.

As Haley Stevens’ Chief of staff for eight years, I speak on behalf of our team in wholeheartedly supporting Abdul El-Sayed for Senate. This election is too important to sow division or stand on the sidelines.

We are shocked and heartbroken by Congresswoman Stevens’ decision
title: Democrats condemn Haley Stevens’ ‘betrayal’ following endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers – US politics live

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Ibstock, which has cut production by a fifth, criticises government for delay in help for housing sector

Sales at the UK’s largest brickmaker plunged by more than a fifth over the summer, as it criticised the government for not introducing fresh help for the housing sector faster.

Leicestershire-based Ibstock said on Monday that sales slumped by 22% below its expectations in the quarter to the end of September, prompting it to slash production levels by a fifth.

Continue reading...
title: UK’s largest brickmaker hit by sales slump as housebuilding downturn deepens

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Airline also weighs up increasing use of AI as part of cost-cutting measures to offset impact of Iran war

Ryanair is considering cost-cutting measures including implementing pay freezes, reducing crew on flights and increasing the use of AI to offset soaring fuel costs because of the Middle East conflict.

Europe’s biggest low-cost carrier said it expects European airlines to raise their ticket prices by as much as 20%, as it anticipates its jet fuel costs will increase by about €2bn (£1.6bn) in its next financial year, which ends in March 2028.

Continue reading...
title: Ryanair considers pay freezes and reducing crew on flights as fuel costs soar

author: Frances Mao
description:
In Ukraine, the app started to send out alarming fake messages late on Sunday night

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of key events in Europe.

Ukraine and Russia have reported corresponding cyber-hacks on their app warning systems overnight.

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine and Russia say emergency air-raid warning systems hit by cyber-hacks – Europe live

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Woman among hundreds asking why electronic trackers not fitted before offenders leave prison

A domestic violence survivor who was punched, threatened with a knife and had her front door kicked in by her former partner is “living in terror” because he has still not been fitted with a tracking tag, weeks after his release from prison.

Michelle, 38, who now lives in a static caravan with her four children, said relatives were sleeping on her floor in case the man tried to attack again. He had been recalled to prison on several occasions before for breaching his probation conditions.

Continue reading...
title: Domestic violence survivor living ‘in terror’ after attacker released without tag

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Australia’s central bank expected to hit mortgage holders again on Tuesday, as war in Middle East combines with collapsing house prices

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s economy is set for a “sharper, longer slowdown”, major bank economists say, as the Reserve Bank is forced to keep interest rates higher to rid the nation of persistent inflationary pressures.

The RBA is widely expected to hit mortgage holders with a fifth rate hike on Tuesday, in a move that will push the cash rate to its highest since 2008 amid rising worries the economy could even be tipped into recession.

Continue reading
title: ‘Sharper, longer slowdown’ predicted for economy as fifth interest rate hike looms

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Frustration grows over the economy with one Labor MP saying voter anger is already high ahead of Reserve Bank of Australia decision

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The NSW premier, Chris Minns, has warned an expected interest rate increase will force job losses and cause businesses to close, insisting the federal government and states should rein in spending to take pressure off the economy.

The intervention from the leader of the country’s biggest state will heap yet more pressure on the Albanese government ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia’s cash rate decision on Tuesday.
title: Minns warns expected RBA rate rise will see ‘shops close that don’t reopen’ as pressure mounts on PM

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Survey finds UK government’s decision to impose trade ban was not a decisive factor in how Israelis voted in election

The UK government’s decision to impose a ban on trade in goods from illegal settlements was not decisive in how Israelis voted in their general election, but a majority think the Israeli government’s settlements policy should change if it is going to lead to further sanctions, a new poll of Israelis shows.

There had been fierce criticism of the UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband’s decision in September to impose a trade ban and wider sanctions on illegal settlements, with some claiming it would drive Israeli voters into the arms of Benjamin Netanyahu.
title: Most Israelis think settlements policy should change to avoid more sanctions, poll finds

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Judicial commission finds against Vicky Prapas over a series of comments, including one made when school children were present

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A magistrate who told a court user “I want to slap you around a bit, too” has come under fire for her offensive and inappropriate language.

The remark was one of several made by Victorian magistrate Vicky Prapas that the state’s judicial watchdog has found to be inappropriate.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I want to slap you around a bit, too’: Victorian magistrate reprimanded over language in court

author: Nick Visser
description:
‘I’m just happy to catch fish,’ Matthew Maurice says after landing 80cm barramundi as part of Northern Territory competition

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Darwin man is $1m richer after angling an 80cm, red-tagged barramundi during a night-time fishing trip with his brother.

Matthew Maurice, a 26-year-old from the Northern Territory, had finished football training and decided to take a boat out on Thursday evening with his sibling, who was visiting from overseas.

Continue reading...
title: Million-dollar fish caught by Darwin man ‘just fishing and talking’ at night with brother

author: Ima Caldwell and Penry Buckley
description:
Deployments of surveillance vans over five months result in nine false alerts and led officers to engage with 146 registered sex offenders

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

More than a million people have had their faces scanned in a trial of real-time facial recognition technology in Western Australia, resulting in 122 arrests and nine incorrect alerts.

WA police said under the five-month trial, which concluded on Saturday, the technology scanned 1,380,882 faces after 100 deployments across 43 regional and metropolitan locations.

Continue reading...
title: Police use facial recognition to scan one million faces in WA trial leading to 122 arrests

author: Roque Planas
description:
President again took aim at progressive Senate candidate and lauded Haley Stevens for endorsing Mike Rogers

Donald Trump railed against Democratic US senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed at a campaign event in Iowa Sunday, repeatedly referring to the Michigan progressive as a “jihadist”.

Trump’s comments aimed to influence a neck-and-neck race that will play an outsized role in determining which party controls the senate after Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Continue reading...
title: Trump launches racist diatribe against Abdul El-Sayed at Iowa rally
